learn.title: Two operations on $x$
learn.body: In $2x+3=11$ the variable has two things done to it: it is multiplied by 2, then 3 is added. To solve, undo them in the reverse order. Subtract first, then divide.

learn.title: Solve $2x+3=11$
learn.body: Undo the addition, then the multiplication.

learn.title: Solve $3x-5=16$
learn.body: The 5 is subtracted, so add it back first.

learn.title: With a division
learn.body: For $\frac{x}{4}+2=5$, subtract 2 to get $\frac{x}{4}=3$. Then multiply both sides by 4 to get $x=12$. Always peel off the added or subtracted number first.

learn.title: With a negative
learn.body: Solving $-2x+1=9$: subtract 1 to get $-2x=8$, then divide by $-2$. Dividing 8 by $-2$ gives $-4$, so $x=-4$. Check: $-2\times(-4)+1=9$.
Work backwards: the last operation done to $x$ is the first one you undo.

questions.prompt: What is the first step to solve $2x+3=11$?
questions.explanation: Undo the addition first, leaving $2x=8$. Then divide.
Add 5 to get $3x=21$, then divide by 3.

questions.prompt: To solve $\frac{x}{4}+2=5$, first subtract \_\_ from both sides.
questions.explanation: Subtract 2 to get $\frac{x}{4}=3$, then multiply by 4 to get $x=12$.

questions.prompt: Solve $5x+3=-12$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Undo the addition, then the multiplication. Check: $5\times(-3)+3=-12$.
